validated_results.title: The Impact of Nutrient Supply on Prostate Cancer Risk Worldwide.
validated_results.reason: Original ecological analysis of national animal protein supply and age-standardized prostate cancer incidence rates across 150 countries.

extraction.comparison_type: per-unit increase in average animal protein supply (AAPS) in regression on age-standardized incidence rate

sample_size.excerpt: We utilized national nutrient supply data from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations for 150 countries, including the average supply of total protein (APS), animal protein (AAPS), fat (AFS), animal protein/total protein ratio (ATR), and share of dietary energy supply derived from cereals, roots, and tubers (CR).

effect_size.excerpt: After adjusting for confounders, regression analysis showed linear relationships between the AAPS (β = 0.605, p = 0.006), ATR (β = 70.76, p = 0.005), CR (β = -1.4451, p < 0.01), and age-standardized incidence rates (ASIRs) of prostate cancer, while no association was observed with APS (β = 0.030, p = 0.483) or AFS (β = 0.237, p = 0.405).

p_value.excerpt: After adjusting for confounders, regression analysis showed linear relationships between the AAPS (β = 0.605, p = 0.006), ATR (β = 70.76, p = 0.005), CR (β = -1.4451, p < 0.01), and age-standardized incidence rates (ASIRs) of prostate cancer, while no association was observed with APS (β = 0.030, p = 0.483) or AFS (β = 0.237, p = 0.405).

design.excerpt: Correlation, regression analyses, and subgroup analysis were conducted.

sample_size.excerpt: To evaluate the association between dairy intake patterns and the risk of prostate cancer (PC), and its histological differentiation, among men from Mexico City. We analyzed the information from 394 incident PC cases paired by age (± 5 years) with 794 population controls.
